expression.expressionFunctionDesc_year: Extracts the year from a date.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_month: Extracts the month (1-12) from a date.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_day: Extracts the day (1-31) from a date.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_quarter: Extracts the quarter of the year (1-4) from a date.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_week: Extracts the ISO week number from a date.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_dayofweek: Extracts the weekday number, from Sunday 0 to Saturday 6.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_dayofyear: Extracts the day number within the year (1-366).
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_hour: Extracts the hour from a date-time value.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_minute: Extracts the minute from a date-time value.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_second: Extracts the second from a date-time value.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_date_diff: Calculates the difference between two dates in the specified unit. Part can be 'day', 'month', 'year', etc.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_date_trunc: Truncates a date to the specified precision. Useful for aligning dates before aggregation by year/month/day.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_strftime: Formats a date or timestamp as a string using the specified format.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_last_day: Returns the last day of the month containing the date.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_parse_date: Parses a string into a date using strptime format syntax. Formats like '%Y-%m-%d', '%Y%m%d'.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_current_date: Returns the current system date. No arguments.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_now: Returns the current system date and time. No arguments.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_ceil: Rounds up to the nearest integer greater than or equal to the argument.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_floor: Rounds down to the nearest integer less than or equal to the argument.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_trunc: Truncates a number to the specified decimal places without rounding.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_sqrt: Returns the square root of a number.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_exp: Returns e raised to the specified power.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_ln: Returns the natural logarithm of a number.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_log10: Returns the base-10 logarithm of a number.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_sign: Returns -1 for negative values, 0 for zero, and 1 for positive values.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_pow: Raises a base number to the specified exponent.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_mod: Returns the remainder after dividing two numbers.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_greatest: Returns the greatest of the supplied comparable values.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_least: Returns the least of the supplied comparable values.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_contains: Checks if a string contains a substring. Returns boolean.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_starts_with: Checks if a string starts with a given prefix. Returns boolean.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_ends_with: Checks if a string ends with a given suffix. Returns boolean.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_replace: Replaces all occurrences of a substring in a string with a new string.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_regexp_replace: Replaces substrings matching a regex pattern in a string.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_regexp_extract: Extracts regex-matched text or a specified capture group.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_regexp_matches: Checks whether a string contains text matching a regular expression.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_lpad: Left-pads a string with a specified character to reach the target length.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_rpad: Right-pads a string with a specified character to reach the target length.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_reverse: Reverses the characters in a string.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_repeat: Repeats a string a specified number of times.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_try_cast: Safely converts an expression to the specified type. Returns NULL on failure instead of throwing an error. Can be used to parse a string into a number, e.g. try_cast([revenue] AS double).
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_abs: Returns the absolute value of a number. Useful for calculating deviations and magnitude of differences.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_round: Rounds a number to the specified decimal places. Defaults to integer when precision is omitted.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_trim: Removes leading and trailing whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines) from a string.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_length: Returns the number of characters in a string (not bytes).
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_substr: Extracts a substring starting at the given position. Position is 1-based. Length is optional.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_splitPart: Splits a string by delimiter and returns the N-th part (1-based). e.g. split_part('a,b,c', ',', 2) → 'b'.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_concat: Concatenates multiple strings into one. Accepts any number of arguments.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_concat_ws: Joins multiple strings with a separator and skips NULL arguments.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_left: Returns the specified number of characters from the left of a string.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_right: Returns the specified number of characters from the right of a string.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_coalesce: Returns the first non-null value from left to right. Commonly used to provide default or fallback values.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_nullif: Returns NULL if the two arguments are equal, otherwise returns the first argument.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_ifnull: Returns a fallback value when the expression is NULL.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_cast: Converts an expression to the specified type. Supports string, int, double, date, timestamp, boolean, etc. Returns NULL on conversion failure.
expression.expressionFunctionDesc_typeof: Returns the data type name of an expression.
expression.expressionFunctionDetailHint: Hover over a function to see details

setupGuide.title: Follow these steps to connect
setupGuide.testTitle: Final step: send a test message

intro.feishu: This usually takes 5–10 minutes. Create and publish a bot app in Feishu first, then return to Sophron, enter the credentials, save, and start the service.
intro.dingtalk: Create an internal app in DingTalk, add a bot, choose the same Stream or Webhook mode selected here, then return to Sophron and enter the app credentials.
intro.wecom: Create a WeCom AI bot in API mode, choose a long connection or URL callback, then enter the matching credentials in Sophron.

prerequisite.feishu: You need permission to create a custom app in the current Feishu tenant. Ask an administrator to create the app or grant developer access if needed.
prerequisite.dingtalk: You must belong to a DingTalk organization and have app-development access. Contact the organization administrator if you cannot create an app.
prerequisite.wecom: Administrators can use WeCom Admin. Members can open Workbench → AI Bot. Ask an administrator to allow bot creation if API mode is unavailable.

createApp.title: Create a custom app
createApp.description: Sign in to Feishu Open Platform, select your tenant, and create a custom app with a recognizable name, description, and icon.
createApp.path: Feishu Open Platform → Developer Console → Create custom app
createApp.result: the new app details page opens

addBot.title: Add the bot capability
addBot.description: Open the new app and add the Bot capability. Without this capability, the app cannot appear in Feishu conversations.
addBot.path: App details → Add app capability → Bot
addBot.result: Bot appears in the app capability list

credentials.title: Copy the App ID and App Secret
credentials.description: Copy both app credentials. Return to the Basic setup tab on this page and enter them without leading or trailing spaces.
credentials.path: App details → Credentials & Basic Info → App credentials
credentials.result: both credential fields in Sophron are filled

permissions.title: Enable the required bot permissions
permissions.description: Open Permission Management and enable every permission below. If bulk import is available, copy and paste the complete list.
permissions.path: App details → Permission Management → Enable / Bulk import

eventsLong.title: Subscribe to messages through a long connection
eventsLong.description: Choose the long-connection event subscription mode, then add the Receive message event. No public callback URL is required.
eventsLong.path: App details → Events & Callbacks → Event configuration → Subscription mode
eventsLong.result: long connection is selected and Receive message is listed

eventsWebhook.title: Configure the webhook and subscribe to messages
eventsWebhook.description: Choose callback URL mode, enter the public webhook URL below, pass URL verification, and add the Receive message event.
eventsWebhook.path: App details → Events & Callbacks → Event configuration → Request URL
eventsWebhook.result: the callback URL passes verification and Receive message is listed

publish.title: Create a version, set availability, and publish
publish.description: Create an app version containing the bot, permissions, and event setup. Add the users or departments that may use it, then submit and publish.
publish.path: App details → Version Management & Release → Create version
publish.result: the version is published and target users are in its availability scope

finish.title: Return to Sophron, save, and start
finish.description: Review the credentials and connection mode in Basic setup, click Save configuration, then use Start service at the top of the page.
finish.result: the Feishu channel status changes to Connected

createApp.title: Create an internal app
createApp.description: Sign in to DingTalk Developer Console, select the organization that will use the bot, and create an internal app with a name and description.
createApp.path: DingTalk Developer Console → App Development → Create app
createApp.result: the new app details page opens

addBot.title: Add an in-app bot and choose Stream mode
addBot.description: Do not create a custom group webhook used only for notifications. Add the Bot capability inside the app, enable bot configuration, select Stream as the message mode, and publish the bot configuration.
addBot.path: App details → Add app capability → Bot → Bot configuration
addBot.result: the Bot capability is enabled and message mode is Stream

addBotWebhook.title: Add an in-app bot and choose HTTP mode
addBotWebhook.description: Add the Bot capability, set message delivery to HTTP/Webhook, and enter the public HTTPS URL below as the receiving endpoint. Do not use a custom group bot that can only push notifications.
addBotWebhook.path: App details → Add app capability → Bot → Bot configuration → Message delivery mode
addBotWebhook.result: HTTP mode is selected and the public callback URL passes validation

credentials.title: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret
credentials.description: Copy the app credentials. Client ID may also be labeled AppKey, and Client Secret may be labeled AppSecret; these are the new and legacy names for the same values.
credentials.path: App details → Credentials & Basic Info → App credentials
credentials.result: the Client ID and Client Secret are saved

publish.title: Publish an app version and set its availability
publish.description: Create and publish an app version, then add the members or departments that can use the bot. Unpublished apps are generally not visible to ordinary members.
publish.path: App details → Version Management & Release → Create version
publish.result: the version is published and target members are in scope

finish.title: Return to Sophron and enter the credentials
finish.description: Enter the Client ID and Client Secret in Basic setup. Add the RobotCode for OpenAPI fallback delivery, then save and start the remote service.
finish.path: Sophron → Settings → Remote Control → DingTalk → Basic setup
finish.result: the channel status changes to Connected

test.title: Find the bot in DingTalk
test.description: Open a direct conversation with the app bot, or add it to a group. Group messages must @mention the bot.
test.path: DingTalk client → Workbench / Group settings → Bots
test.result: the bot receives the message and replies

prerequisite.title: Confirm that you can create an AI bot
prerequisite.description: Administrators can use WeCom Admin; members can search for AI Bot in Workbench. Ask an administrator to enable bot creation if the button is missing.
prerequisite.path: Admin: Security & Management → Management Tools → AI Bot; Member: Workbench → AI Bot
prerequisite.result: the Create bot button is visible

createBot.title: Create the bot in API mode
createBot.description: Choose Create bot. If the AI-generated flow opens first, choose Manual creation, then API mode. Do not create a basic group webhook bot.
createBot.path: AI Bot → Create bot → Manual creation → Create in API mode
createBot.result: the bot editor displays API configuration

longConnection.title: Set the name, visibility, and long connection
longConnection.description: Name the bot, add permitted members, departments, or tags to its visibility scope, and choose Use long connection under API configuration.
longConnection.path: Bot editor → Available members / Visibility → API configuration → Use long connection
longConnection.result: target users are visible and long connection is selected

webhookConnection.title: Choose URL callback and enter the public endpoint
webhookConnection.description: Choose Use URL callback in API configuration and enter the public HTTPS URL below. The Sophron remote service must be running before the bot configuration is saved.
webhookConnection.path: Bot editor → API configuration → Use URL callback → URL
webhookConnection.result: WeCom can reach the endpoint and URL verification succeeds

credentials.title: Get the Bot ID and Secret, then save
credentials.description: Copy the Bot ID, click Get next to Secret, store the Secret immediately, and save the bot. The full Secret may not remain visible.
credentials.path: Bot editor → API configuration → Configuration method → Bot ID / Secret
credentials.result: the credentials are stored and the bot details page opens

webhookCredentials.title: Generate Token and EncodingAESKey
webhookCredentials.description: Generate a Token and EncodingAESKey in the URL callback settings, then copy both values into Basic setup in Sophron. They protect callback signatures and encryption and must remain private.
webhookCredentials.path: Bot editor → API configuration → URL callback → Token / EncodingAESKey
webhookCredentials.result: Token and EncodingAESKey match exactly in WeCom and Sophron

finish.title: Return to Sophron and enter the credentials
finish.description: Enter the Bot ID and Secret in Basic setup, save, and start the remote control service.
finish.path: Sophron → Settings → Remote Control → WeCom → Basic setup
finish.result: the WeCom channel status changes to Connected

test.title: Add the bot and send a test message
test.description: Find the new bot in WeCom and start a direct conversation, or add it to a group and @mention it before sending a request.
test.path: WeCom client → Contacts / Workbench → AI Bot
test.result: the bot receives the message and replies

test.feishu: Send “Hello” in a direct bot chat. In a group, add the bot and @mention it before sending “Hello.” Receiving a reply from Sophron confirms the connection.
test.dingtalk: Send “Hello” in a direct bot chat. Group tests must @mention the bot. A Sophron reply confirms the selected delivery mode.
test.wecom: Send “Hello” in a direct bot chat or @mention the bot in a group. A reply confirms the selected delivery mode and visibility scope.

warning.feishu: Common causes of no response include an unpublished app, a user outside the availability scope, or a missing im.message.receive_v1 subscription. Keep the App Secret private.
warning.dingtalk: Use an in-app bot. Webhook mode requires a publicly reachable HTTPS endpoint and Sophron must remain running; it is not the custom group webhook used only to push notifications. DingTalk forwards group messages only when the bot is @mentioned.
warning.wecom: A bot can keep only one long connection. Webhook mode requires a publicly reachable HTTPS endpoint and Sophron must remain running. Token, Secret, and EncodingAESKey are sensitive.
